pair.exists_note: Not strictly established. The closest candidate is Q=A2 (R-89 refused) and P=A3 (R-90 issued), on the same ruling. It fails the strict 'differs ONLY in prior state' test on three counts: (a) P's prior state is UNK in the text (unused is inferred, not quoted); (b) the proposer of R-89 is UNK, so 'same actor' is inferred, not attested; (c) the two acts come from one correction event, so they are not two independent acts. Under a lenient reading (accept the inferences) the pair exists.
pair.P: A3: R-90 issued to DISCOVERY BOUNDARY CONFIRMATION (WP-4C-2)
pair.Q: A2: R-89 put forward for the same ruling and refused
pair.separating_variable: Occupancy: whether the identifier is already held by another filed ruling. Not retirement. Not the same variable as 'retired, not recycled', though closely related. Both rules are justified by the same defect ('one number two decisions'). Retirement also works as occupancy that outlasts withdrawal, because the withdrawn row is retained. No refusal on retirement grounds is attested.

clusters_note: Both P and Q come from one decision cluster: the single 'NUMBERING CORRECTION RECORDED AT ISSUE' passage in R-90, with one author and one date. The R-89 row (A1) independently backs up Q's prior state (the number was in fact held), but it is not a second decision on the contrast. The retirement norm (A4/A5) is a separate, later cluster (the withdrawal annotation) and is not part of the pair.
notes: References to R-88 and R-79 are citations of existing rulings, not number-assignment acts, so they are excluded.
The withdrawal of R-90 is a status change of a ruling, not a number assignment. Only the retirement of its number (A4) is counted, as a norm.
Both rows are PREPARED, not ADOPTED. Whether an 'issued' identifier on a PREPARED ruling counts as final issuance is ambiguous.
The retirement norm is stated as a rule for one identifier (R-90), which sits between a NORM-STATEMENT and a particular act.
